bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum Token {
    Str(String),
    Paragraph(Vec<Token>),
    Header(i32, Vec<Token>),
    Emphasis(Vec<Token>),
    Strong(Vec<Token>),
    Strikethrough(Vec<Token>),
    Superscript(Vec<Token>),
    Subscript(Vec<Token>),
    Code(String),
    BlockQuote(Vec<Token>),
    CodeBlock(String, String),
    List(Vec<Token>),
    OrderedList(usize, Vec<Token>),
    Item(Vec<Token>),
    TaskItem(bool, Vec<Token>),
    Link(String, String, Vec<Token>),
    Image(String, String, Vec<Token>),
    StandaloneImage(String, String, Vec<Token>),
    Rule,
    SoftBreak,
    HardBreak,
    FootnoteReference(String),
    FootnoteDefinition(String, Vec<Token>),
    Table(usize, Vec<Token>),
    TableHead(Vec<Token>),
    TableRow(Vec<Token>),
    TableCell(Vec<Token>),
    Html(String),
    /// Raw text that must not be processed further (used for HTML blocks)
    Annotation(String, Vec<Token>),
}

impl Token {
    pub fn is_str(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(*self, Token::Str(_))
    }

    pub fn inner(&self) -> Option<&[Token]> {
        match *self {
            Token::Paragraph(ref v)
            | Token::Header(_, ref v)
            | Token::Emphasis(ref v)
            | Token::Strong(ref v)
            | Token::Strikethrough(ref v)
            | Token::Superscript(ref v)
            | Token::Subscript(ref v)
            | Token::BlockQuote(ref v)
            | Token::List(ref v)
            | Token::OrderedList(_, ref v)
            | Token::Item(ref v)
            | Token::TaskItem(_, ref v)
            | Token::Link(_, _, ref v)
            | Token::Image(_, _, ref v)
            | Token::StandaloneImage(_, _, ref v)
            | Token::FootnoteDefinition(_, ref v)
            | Token::Table(_, ref v)
            | Token::TableHead(ref v)
            | Token::TableRow(ref v)
            | Token::TableCell(ref v)
            | Token::Annotation(_, ref v) => Some(v),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn inner_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Vec<Token>> {
        match *self {
            Token::Paragraph(ref mut v)
            | Token::Header(_, ref mut v)
            | Token::Emphasis(ref mut v)
            | Token::Strong(ref mut v)
            | Token::Strikethrough(ref mut v)
            | Token::Superscript(ref mut v)
            | Token::Subscript(ref mut v)
            | Token::BlockQuote(ref mut v)
            | Token::List(ref mut v)
            | Token::OrderedList(_, ref mut v)
            | Token::Item(ref mut v)
            | Token::TaskItem(_, ref mut v)
            | Token::Link(_, _, ref mut v)
            | Token::Image(_, _, ref mut v)
            | Token::StandaloneImage(_, _, ref mut v)
            | Token::FootnoteDefinition(_, ref mut v)
            | Token::Table(_, ref mut v)
            | Token::TableHead(ref mut v)
            | Token::TableRow(ref mut v)
            | Token::TableCell(ref mut v)
            | Token::Annotation(_, ref mut v) => Some(v),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// Concatenate every `Str` contained in a token tree
pub fn collect_text(tokens: &[Token]) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    for t in tokens {
        match *t {
            Token::Str(ref x) => s.push_str(x),
            Token::Code(ref x) => s.push_str(x),
            Token::SoftBreak | Token::HardBreak => s.push(' '),
            _ => {
                if let Some(inner) = t.inner() {
                    s.push_str(&collect_text(inner));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    s
}
